# Heat pump installer survey analysis

## Section 5 - Productivity

### Foreword

As for all previous section, throughout the analysis, we collapsed responses and respondents to the survey into various subcategories to get the most relevant information. This collapsing was done based on the guidelines laid out in the [analysis plan](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1M1nzdf3fyTjipmaKJKViin0EB3e3R1afOQglwMGJaII/edit){target="_blank"}.

You can find the pre-analysis code to run before analysing section 5 of the installer survey below.

```{r}

# https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVNWK_xBg=/

# Link to the analysis plan
# https://docs.google.com/document/d/1M1nzdf3fyTjipmaKJKViin0EB3e3R1afOQglwMGJaII/edit#heading=h.voghu12g248q

## Set working directory

##### Load dataset

installer_survey_data <- arrow::read_parquet(file_path)

##### Change names of variables to make things easier

##### Recode free text answers

##### Filter out partial responses
data <- data %>%
  filter(x0e_analytical_sample == "TRUE")


##### Pre-analysis - Collapsed options and new variables

## Create employment_type variables
data <- data %>%
  mutate(employment_type = case_when(x5_are_you_responding_to_this_survey_as == "An employee of a firm" ~ "Employee", 
                                     x5_are_you_responding_to_this_survey_as == "A contractor or freelancer" ~ "Contractor or freelancer",
                                     x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own == "I’m a sole trader" ~ "Sole trader",
                                     x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own == "I own a company with 5 or fewer employees" ~ "Company owner", 
                                     x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own == "I own a company with 6-25 employees" ~ "Company owner",
                                     x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own == "I own a company with 26-100 employees" ~ "Company owner",
                                     x6a_what_size_company_do_you_own == "I own a company with over 100 employees" ~ "Company owner", TRUE ~ "Not asked"))
data$employment_type <- as.factor(data$employment_type)

# Create variable where employees and contractors are merged together
data <- data %>%
  mutate(employment_type_soletrader_owner_merged = case_when(employment_type == "Contractor or freelancer" ~ "Contractor or freelancer",
                                                             employment_type == "Employee" ~ "Employee",
                                                             employment_type == "Sole trader" ~ "Sole trader or company owner",
                                                             employment_type == "Company owner" ~ "Sole trader or company owner"))
data$employment_type_soletrader_owner_merged <- as.factor(data$employment_type_soletrader_owner_merged)

# Create variable where employees and contractors are merged together
data <- data %>%
  mutate(employment_type_employee_contractor_merged = case_when(employment_type == "Contractor or freelancer" ~ "Contractor/freelancer or employee",
                                                                employment_type == "Employee" ~ "Contractor/freelancer or employee",
                                                                employment_type == "Sole trader" ~ "Sole trader",
                                                                employment_type == "Company owner" ~ "Company owner"))
data$employment_type_employee_contractor_merged <- as.factor(data$employment_type_employee_contractor_merged)

# Create dummy variable for employment type
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dummy_employment_type = case_when(employment_type == "Employee" ~ "Employee or contractor/freelancer",
                                           employment_type == "Contractor or freelancer" ~ "Employee or contractor/freelancer",
                                           employment_type == "Company owner" ~ "Company owner or sole trader",
                                           employment_type == "Sole trader" ~ "Company owner or sole trader"))
data$dummy_employment_type <- as.factor(data$dummy_employment_type)

# Create dummy for contractors and freelancers
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dummy_contractors = case_when(employment_type == "Contractor or freelancer" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0))

# Create dummy for employees
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dummy_employees = case_when(employment_type == "Employee" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0))

# Create dummy for sole traders

# Create dummy for company owner
data <- data %>%
  mutate(dummy_company_owner = case_when(employment_type == "Company owner" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0))


##### Participant age

                                       "18-24" = "34 and under",
                                       "25-34" = "34 and under",
                                       "35-44" = "35-44",

                                                    "Less than 12 months" = "Under 3 years",
                                                    "1-3 years" = "Under 3 years",
                                                    "3-5 years" = "3-5 years",
                                                    "5-10 years" = "5-10 years",
                                                    "10-20 years" = "Over 10 years",
                                                    "Over 20 years" = "Over 10 years"))

##### Distance travelled for work

## Questions 30a and 30b
# Installers were asked if they have done any retrofit or new build (select all that apply format)
# Some responded only retrofit, other only new build, others both.
# Those who replied retrofit and new build were asked q33, what is the majority of your installations.
# To create variable retrofit_newbuild we want to include those who only responded retrofit to q30 and those who responded retrofit to q33.

# Filter the "only retrofit answers"
# To do this, I find answers which contain "retrofit" which include those who replied retrofit and retrofit, new build.
# Then I create a new variable with condition 1 = retrofit in new variable and condition 2 = not asked (q33) since those who replied only retrofit to q30 were not asked q33.
# This way I have a binary variable which takes the value "retrofit" for installers who replied "retrofit" only to q30.

# This follows the guidelines in the pre-analysis plan.

# Separate vector
data$x30a_answer1 <- sapply(data$x30a_has_your_business_done_any_retrofit_or_new_build_heat_pump_installations_over_the_last_12_months_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[1]))
data$x30a_answer2 <- sapply(data$x30a_has_your_business_done_any_retrofit_or_new_build_heat_pump_installations_over_the_last_12_months_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[2]))

# Step 1
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_retrofit_q30a = ifelse(str_detect(x30a_answer1, fixed("Retrofit")) |
                                      str_detect(x30a_answer2, fixed("Retrofit")), 1, 0)) 
# I have a dummy variable that takes the value 1 if respondents replied retrofit only or retrofit and new build to q30a.

# Step 2
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(retrofit_only_owners = case_when(dummy_retrofit_q30a == 1 & x33a_over_the_past_12_months_where_has_the_majority_of_the_heat_pump_installations_your_business_has_done_been == "Not asked" ~ "Retrofit only", TRUE ~ NA_character_))
# I have a dummy variable that takes the value retrofit only for the respondent who only do retrofit work.

# Do the same for new build
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_newbuild_q30a = ifelse(str_detect(x30a_answer1, fixed("New build")) |
                                      str_detect(x30a_answer2, fixed("New build")), 1, 0))
# I have a dummy variable that takes the value 1 if respondents replied new build only or retrofit and new build to q30a.

# Step 2
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(newbuild_only_owners = case_when(dummy_newbuild_q30a == 1 & x33a_over_the_past_12_months_where_has_the_majority_of_the_heat_pump_installations_your_business_has_done_been == "Not asked" ~ "Newbuild only", TRUE ~ NA_character_))
# I have a dummy variable that takes the value new build only for the respondent who only do new build work.

# Create a summary retrofit_newbuild variable
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(retrofit_newbuild_owners = case_when(retrofit_only_owners == "Retrofit only" ~ "Retrofit only",
                                              newbuild_only_owners == "Newbuild only" ~ "New build only",
                                              x30a_answer1 == "Not asked" ~ NA_character_,
                                              TRUE ~ "Both retrofit and new build"))

## retrofit_newbuild variable for sole traders, employees, and contractors
# Separate vector
data$x30b_answer1 <- sapply(data$x30b_have_you_done_any_retrofit_or_new_build_heat_pump_installations_over_the_last_12_months_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[1]))
data$x30b_answer2 <- sapply(data$x30b_have_you_done_any_retrofit_or_new_build_heat_pump_installations_over_the_last_12_months_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[2]))

# Step 1
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_retrofit_q30b = ifelse(str_detect(x30b_answer1, fixed("Retrofit")) |
                                      str_detect(x30b_answer2, fixed("Retrofit")), 1, 0)) 
# I have a dummy variable that takes the value 1 if respondents replied retrofit only or retrofit and new build to q30b.

# Step 2
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(retrofit_only_others = case_when(dummy_retrofit_q30b == 1 & x33b_over_the_past_12_months_where_has_the_majority_of_your_heat_pump_installation_work_been == "Not asked" ~ "Retrofit only", TRUE ~ NA_character_))
# I have a dummy variable that takes the value retrofit only for the respondent who only do retrofit work.

# Do the same for new build
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_newbuild_q30b = ifelse(str_detect(x30b_answer1, fixed("New build")) |
                                      str_detect(x30b_answer2, fixed("New build")), 1, 0))
# I have a dummy variable that takes the value 1 if respondents replied new build only or retrofit and new build to q30b.

# Step 2
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(newbuild_only_others = case_when(dummy_newbuild_q30b == 1 & x33b_over_the_past_12_months_where_has_the_majority_of_your_heat_pump_installation_work_been == "Not asked" ~ "Newbuild only", TRUE ~ NA_character_))
# I have a dummy variable that takes the value new build only for the respondent who only do new build work.

# Create a summary retrofit_newbuild variable
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(retrofit_newbuild_others = case_when(retrofit_only_others == "Retrofit only" ~ "Retrofit only",
                                              newbuild_only_others == "Newbuild only" ~ "New build only",
                                              x30b_answer1 == "Not asked" ~ NA_character_,
                                              TRUE ~ "Both retrofit and new build"))

# Merge variables for all installers
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(retrofit_newbuild_all = coalesce(retrofit_newbuild_owners, retrofit_newbuild_others))
data$retrofit_newbuild_all <- as.factor(data$retrofit_newbuild_all)
```

### Functions

```{r}
## Create function to get summary table
generate_table <- function(data, variable1, variable2) {
  table_result <- xtabs(~ data[[variable1]] + data[[variable2]], data)
  table_result <- as.data.frame.matrix(table_result)
  table_result$total_row <- rowSums(table_result)
  column_totals <- colSums(table_result, na.rm = TRUE)
  total_row <- as.data.frame(t(column_totals))
  row_name <- "total_col"
  rownames(total_row)[1] <- row_name
  table_result <- rbind(table_result, total_row)
}


## Create function to export all data frames in CSV
export_to_csv <- function(data_frame, file_name) {
  write.csv(data_frame, file_name, row.names = TRUE)
}
```

#### 5.01 \| How many heat pumps did survey participants install in the last 12 months?

Figure 5.1a shows the distribution of the number of heat pump installations completed over the past 12 months by employment type.

```{r}
# Create dataframe
plot_5.1a <- data %>%
  drop_na(x37_all_collapsed, employment_type) %>%
  count(x37_all_collapsed, employment_type) %>%
  rename(count = n)

# Plot distribution
ggplot(plot_5.1a, aes(x = x37_all_collapsed, y = count, fill = employment_type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Figure 5.1a. Distribution of the number of heat pump installations \nin the past 12 months by employment type (all installers)",
       x = "",
       y = "Count",
       fill = "Employment type") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 150, by = 20)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 15)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = wes_palette("Zissou1"))
```

```{r}
# Alternative plot
ggplot(plot_5.1a, aes(x = x37_all_collapsed, y = count, fill = employment_type)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge", stat = "identity") +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(count > 0, as.character(count), "")),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Figure 5.1a. Distribution of the number of heat pump installations \nin the past 12 months by employment type (all installers)",
       x = "",
       y = "Count",
       fill = "Employment type") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 70, by = 10)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 15)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = wes_palette("Zissou1"))
```

#### 5.04 \| How does the number of heat pumps that survey participants install differ depending on whether they only, or mostly, do work in retrofit, or only, or mostly, do work in new builds?

Next we want to know if the number of installations varies if installers do mostly retrofit or new build work. To do so, we cross the answers to question 37a and 37b with the answers to questions about the ratio between retrofit and new build work. We create a new binary variable that takes the value "Retrofit" if installers answered that they only do retrofit or mostly do retrofit if they do both, and "New build" otherwise. The distribution is as follows: 264 installers do only or mostly retrofit, and 81 installers do only or mostly new build. Figure 5.4a shows the distribution for all installers.

```{r}
# Create new binary variable
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_retrofit_newbuild_all = case_when(retrofit_newbuild_all == "Retrofit only" ~ "Retrofit",
                                                 retrofit_newbuild_all == "New build only" ~ "New build",
                                                 x33a_over_the_past_12_months_where_has_the_majority_of_the_heat_pump_installations_your_business_has_done_been == "Retrofit" ~ "Retrofit",
                                                 x33b_over_the_past_12_months_where_has_the_majority_of_your_heat_pump_installation_work_been == "Retrofit" ~ "Retrofit",
                                                 x33a_over_the_past_12_months_where_has_the_majority_of_the_heat_pump_installations_your_business_has_done_been == "New build" ~ "New build",
                                                 x33b_over_the_past_12_months_where_has_the_majority_of_your_heat_pump_installation_work_been == "New build" ~ "New build"))
data$dummy_retrofit_newbuild_all <- as.factor(data$dummy_retrofit_newbuild_all)

# Create data frame
plot_5.4a <- data %>%
  drop_na(x37_all_collapsed, dummy_retrofit_newbuild_all) %>%
  count(x37_all_collapsed, dummy_retrofit_newbuild_all) %>%
  rename(count = n)

# Plot distribution
ggplot(plot_5.4a, aes(x = x37_all_collapsed, y = count, fill = dummy_retrofit_newbuild_all)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Figure 5.4a. Distribution of the number of heat pump installations \nin the past 12 months by type of work (all installers)",
       x = "",
       y = "Count",
       fill = "Type of work") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 160, by = 20)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 15)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = wes_palette("Zissou1"))
```

#### 5.05 \| Are there differences in the number of installations done by those who are and aren’t MCS certified?

We also want to know if the distribution varies whether installers are MCS certified or not. To do so, we cross the answers to questions 37a and 37b with answers to questions 21 "Are you (if sole trader, employee or contractor) or is your business (if company owner) MCS certified?". In this case, all answers other than "Yes" are coded as not being MCS certified (101 installers are MCS certified and 244 are not MCS certified). Figure 5.5a shows the distribution for all installers.

```{r}
# Create dummy MCS variable
data <- data %>%
```

#### 5.06 \| How do the number of installations that survey participants do vary depending on the method that they use to MCS-certify their installations?

In this case, we cannot merge questions 36a, 36b, 36c, and 36d together because different categories of installers were presented different options. Therefore, we provide a plot for each employment type: company owners, sole traders, employees, and contractors. Keep in mind that installers were able to select more than one option, therefore the total count of installers in this case may be greater than 163. Figure 5.6a shows the distribution for company owners (n=163).

```{r}
# Code from script 4
# Separate answers
data$x36a_answer1 <- sapply(data$x36a_in_your_businesss_retrofit_work_does_your_business_install_heat_pumps_through_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[1]))
data$x36a_answer2 <- sapply(data$x36a_in_your_businesss_retrofit_work_does_your_business_install_heat_pumps_through_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[2]))
data$x36a_answer3 <- sapply(data$x36a_in_your_businesss_retrofit_work_does_your_business_install_heat_pumps_through_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[3]))
# No respondents select more than 3 options.

# Create dummy variables for each possible answer
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_MCS_certified_owners = ifelse(str_detect(x36a_answer1, fixed("My firm’s MCS certification")) |
                                             str_detect(x36a_answer2, fixed("My firm’s MCS certification")) |
                                             str_detect(x36a_answer3, fixed("My firm’s MCS certification")), 1, 0))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_sign_off_owners = ifelse(str_detect(x36a_answer1, fixed("With sign off from another MCS certified firm")) |
                                        str_detect(x36a_answer2, fixed("With sign off from another MCS certified firm")) |
                                        str_detect(x36a_answer3, fixed("With sign off from another MCS certified firm")), 1, NA_integer_)) # used different end of code because created different values when no sign off value.

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_umbrella_scheme_owners = ifelse(str_detect(x36a_answer1, fixed("An MCS umbrella scheme")) |
                                               str_detect(x36a_answer2, fixed("An MCS umbrella scheme")) |
                                               str_detect(x36a_answer3, fixed("An MCS umbrella scheme")), 1, 0))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_without_MCS_owners = ifelse(str_detect(x36a_answer1, fixed("Without MCS certification")) |
                                           str_detect(x36a_answer2, fixed("Without MCS certification")) |
                                           str_detect(x36a_answer3, fixed("Without MCS certification")), 1, 0))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_other_owners = ifelse(str_detect(x36a_answer1, fixed("Other")) |
                                     str_detect(x36a_answer2, fixed("Other")) |
                                     str_detect(x36a_answer3, fixed("Other")), 1, 0))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_dont_know_owners = ifelse(str_detect(x36a_answer1, fixed("Don't know")) |
                                         str_detect(x36a_answer2, fixed("Don't know")) |
                                         str_detect(x36a_answer3, fixed("Don't know")), 1, 0))

# Create a new dataframe with only the dummy variables above
subset_dummy <- data %>%
    filter(employment_type == "Company owner") %>% 
    select(dummy_MCS_certified_owners, dummy_sign_off_owners, dummy_umbrella_scheme_owners, dummy_without_MCS_owners, dummy_other_owners, dummy_dont_know_owners, x37_all)

# Replace NAs by 0
subset_dummy <- subset_dummy %>%
  mutate_if(is.numeric, ~replace(., is.na(.), 0)) # numeric because x37_all is factor and does not have NA

# New code
# Create summary table
table <- subset_dummy %>%
  group_by(x37_all) %>%
  summarise(
    count_dummy_MCS_certified_owners = sum(dummy_MCS_certified_owners),
    count_dummy_sign_off_owners = sum(dummy_sign_off_owners),
    count_dummy_umbrella_scheme_owners = sum(dummy_umbrella_scheme_owners),
    count_dummy_without_MCS_owners = sum(dummy_without_MCS_owners),
    count_dummy_other_owners = sum(dummy_other_owners),
    count_dummy_dont_know_owners = sum(dummy_dont_know_owners))

# Reshape the data to long format
plot_5.6a <- table %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("count_d"), names_to = "count_dummy", values_to = "count_value")

# Rename variables in the summary_table
plot_5.6a <- plot_5.6a %>%
  mutate(count_dummy = case_when(
    count_dummy == "count_dummy_MCS_certified_owners" ~ "My firm’s MCS certification",
    count_dummy == "count_dummy_sign_off_owners" ~ "With sign off from another MCS certified firm",
    count_dummy == "count_dummy_umbrella_scheme_owners" ~ "An MCS umbrella scheme",
    count_dummy == "count_dummy_without_MCS_owners" ~ "Without MCS certification",
    count_dummy == "count_dummy_other_owners" ~ "Other",
    count_dummy == "count_dummy_dont_know_owners" ~ "Don't know"))


# Order labels
order_labels <- c("My firm’s MCS certification",
                  "With sign off from another MCS certified firm",
                  "An MCS umbrella scheme",
                  "Without MCS certification",
                  "Other",
                  "Don't know")

# Convert count_dummy to a factor with desired order
plot_5.6a$count_dummy <- factor(plot_5.6a$count_dummy, levels = order_labels)

# Plot
ggplot(plot_5.6a, aes(x = count_dummy, y = count_value, fill = x37_all)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Figure 5.6a. Distribution of the number of installations in the past 12 months \nby the methods that they use to MCS-certify their installations (company owners)",
       x = "",
       y = "Count of installers",
       fill = "Number of installations") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 10)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues")
```

```{r}
# Code from script 4
# Separate answers
```

```{r}
data$x36d_answer2 <- sapply(data$x36d_in_your_retrofit_work_do_you_install_heat_pumps_through_select_all_that_apply, function(x) as.character(x[2]))
# No respondents select more than 2 options.

# Create dummy variables for each possible answer

  mutate(dummy_MCS_certified_contractors = ifelse(str_detect(x36d_answer1, fixed("My own MCS certification")) |
                                                  str_detect(x36d_answer2, fixed("My own MCS certification")), 1, 0))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_firm_certification_contractors = ifelse(str_detect(x36d_answer1, fixed("The MCS certification of the business I’m working for")) |
                                                       str_detect(x36d_answer2, fixed("The MCS certification of the business I’m working for")), 1, 0))

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_umbrella_scheme_contractors = ifelse(str_detect(x36d_answer1, fixed("The MCS umbrella scheme of the business I’m working for")) |

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_without_MCS_contractors = ifelse(str_detect(x36d_answer1, fixed("Without MCS certification")) |

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(dummy_other_contractors = ifelse(str_detect(x36d_answer1, fixed("Other")) |

data <- data %>%

# Create a new dataframe with only the dummy variables above

    filter(employment_type == "Contractor or freelancer") %>%

# New code

  group_by(x37_all) %>%
  summarise(
    count_dummy_MCS_certified_contractors = sum(dummy_MCS_certified_contractors),
    count_dummy_firm_certification_contractors = sum(dummy_firm_certification_contractors),

    count_dummy_dont_know_contractors = sum(dummy_dont_know_contractors))

# Reshape the data to long format

# Rename variables in the summary_table

  mutate(count_dummy = case_when(
```

#### 5.08 \| Do survey participants want to increase, reduce, or maintain the number of heat pumps they install each year?

Figure 5.8a shows the distribution of installers' preferences regarding the number of heat pump installations they want to do in the future for all installers (n=345).

```{r}
# Turn "not asked" into NA's for q38a and q38b to merge them into a single variable
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x38a_bis = recode(x38a_would_you_like_your_business_to_install_more_heat_pumps_each_year_id_like_to_install, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x38b_bis = recode(x38b_would_you_like_to_install_more_heat_pumps_each_year_id_like_to_install, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(x38_all = coalesce(x38a_bis, x38b_bis))

# Create dataframe
plot_5.8a <- data %>%
  drop_na(x38_all) %>%
  count(x38_all) %>%
  rename(count = n)

# Plot for all installers
ggplot(data, aes(x = x38_all)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "blue") +
  geom_text(stat='count', aes(label=after_stat(count)), vjust=-0.5, size = 3) + 
  labs(title = "Figure 5.8a. Distribution of installers' preferences for numbers of heat pump \ninstallations in the future", 
       x = "", 
       y = "Count") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 200, by = 20)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 15),
                   limits = c("Far fewer heat pumps",
                              "Fewer heat pumps",
                              "The same amount of heat pumps",
                              "More heat pumps",
                              "Far more heat pumps",
                              "Don't know"))
```

#### 5.11 \| What’s the main reason survey participants give for wanting to reduce the number of heat pumps they install?

We want to understand what the biggest reason for wanting to install fewer heat pumps is for installers. Note that this is a small group of respondents (n=13). Only sole traders and company owners were asked about the reasons. Three installers who wish to install fewer (n=1) or far fewer (n=2) heat pumps are therefore dropped. Figure 5.11 shows the distribution for 10 installers in total.

```{r}
# Turn "not asked" into NA's to merge them into a single variable
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x39a_bis = recode(x39a_whats_the_biggest_reason_you_have_for_wanting_to_reduce_the_number_of_heat_pumps_you_install_please_select_one_option, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>%
  mutate(x39b_bis = recode(x39b_whats_the_biggest_reason_you_have_for_wanting_to_reduce_the_number_of_heat_pumps_you_install_please_select_one_option, "Not asked" = NA_character_))
data <- data %>% 
  mutate(x39_all = coalesce(x39a_bis, x39b_bis))

# Create data frame
# Generate a complete set of levels
all_levels <- data.frame(x39_all = unique(data$x39_all))
plot_5.11 <- data %>%
  drop_na(x39_all) %>%
  count(x39_all) %>%
  rename(count = n) %>%
  complete(x39_all = all_levels$x39_all, fill = list(count = 0)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(x39_all))

# Plot for all installers
ggplot(data %>% filter(!is.na(x39_all)), aes(x = x39_all)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "blue") +
  geom_text(stat='count', aes(label=after_stat(count)), vjust=-0.5, size = 3) + 
  labs(title = "Figure 5.11. Distribution of the reason why installers wish to install fewer or \nfar fewer heat pumps in the future (sole traders and company owners)", 
       x = "", 
       y = "Count") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 5, by = 1), limits = c(0,4)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 10),
                   limits = c("Heat pumps are less profitable than other work",
                              "Heat pump installations are harder jobs than other kinds of work", 
                              "I am unable to find suitable staff to work with on heat pump installations", 
                              "I am unable to source the hardware I need, or I am unable to source it in a timely fashion", 
                              "I don’t believe there is sufficient government support for the heat pump sector", 
                              "I believe that other renewable technologies are currently better", 
                              "I believe that other fossil fuel technologies are currently better", 
                              "Other", 
                              "Don't know"))
```

The following two plots were added during ASF team workshop (18 April). Figure 5.12a shows the distribution by time in the sector for sole traders and company owners who responded that they want to install more or far more heat pumps in the future (n=170).

```{r}
## Create a function to create data frame (employment type)
create_df_two <- function(data, variable1, variable2) {
  data %>% 
    drop_na({{ variable1 }}, {{ variable2 }}) %>%
    count({{ variable1 }}, {{ variable2 }}) %>%
    rename(count = n)
}
## Create a function to plot (dodge) the distribution by employment type
create_plot_dodge <- function(data, variable1, variable2, fill_label, title) {
  
  ggplot(data, aes_string(x = variable1, y = "count", fill = variable2)) +
    geom_bar(position = "dodge", stat = "identity") +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(count > 0, as.character(count), "0")),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
    labs(title = title, x = "", y = "Count", fill = fill_label) +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 300, by = 10)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = label_wrap_gen(width = 12), limits = levels_order) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues")
}
## Create function to get summary table
generate_table <- function(data, variable1, variable2) {
  table_result <- xtabs(~ data[[variable1]] + data[[variable2]], data)
  table_result <- as.data.frame.matrix(table_result)
  table_result$total_row <- rowSums(table_result)
  column_totals <- colSums(table_result, na.rm = TRUE)
  total_row <- as.data.frame(t(column_totals))
  row_name <- "total_col"
  rownames(total_row)[1] <- row_name
  table_result <- rbind(table_result, total_row)
}
## Create function to export all data frames in CSV
export_to_csv <- function(data_frame, file_name) {
  write.csv(data_frame, file_name, row.names = TRUE)
}

# Create data frame
plot_5.12a <- create_df_two(data, x40_all, length_hp_sector_collapsed)

# Plot
levels_order <- c("I have too little customer demand", 
  "Other work in my business’s repertoire is more attractive (e.g. bathrooms, batteries, etc.)", 
  "I am not able to source the hardware I need, or I am not able to source it in a timely fashion", 
  "I am unable to find additional suitable staff", 
  "I find that ‘unnecessary’ elements of installation or admin take up so much time that my business is prevented from doing more jobs",
  "No barriers",
  "Other")
create_plot_dodge(data = plot_5.12a, 
                  variable1 = "x40_all", 
                  variable2 = "length_hp_sector_collapsed",
                  fill_label = "Time in sector",
                  title = "Figure. Distribution of the biggest barrier to installing heat pumps \nin the future by time in sector (sole traders and company owners)")

# Create summary table
plot_5.12a <- generate_table(data, "length_hp_sector_collapsed", "x40_all")

# Export csv
export_to_csv(plot_5.12a, "plot_5.12a.csv")
```

#### 5.40 \| How does the way survey participants feel about the amount of time they spend on business management differ depending on the size of the company they own and the number of installations they’ve done over the last 12 months?

The last 12 questions examine the distribution of installers' attitudes towards different aspect of their work by size of company and number of installations. As these are all categorical variables, there is a large number of possible combinations. In the first case below, there exist 80 combinations (with the collapsed version of variables) when interacting company size and number of installations.

Therefore, we decided to produce CSV files which give the count of installers for each combination but we do not plot the results.

```{r}
# Create data frame (collapsed)
subset_2 <- data %>% 
  filter(employment_type %in% c("Company owner", "Sole trader")) %>% 
  select(x41_all_business_management, x37_all_collapsed, size_company_owned_collapsed_1)

plot_5.40a <- subset_2 %>%
  drop_na(x41_all_business_management, x37_all_collapsed, size_company_owned_collapsed_1) %>%
  count(x41_all_business_management, x37_all_collapsed, size_company_owned_collapsed_1) %>%
  rename(count = n)

# Create a data frame with all combinations
all_combinations <- expand.grid(x41_all_business_management = unique(plot_5.40a$x41_all_business_management),
                                size_company_owned_collapsed_1 = unique(plot_5.40a$size_company_owned_collapsed_1),
                                x37_all_collapsed = unique(plot_5.40a$x37_all_collapsed))

# Merge with original data to get counts
plot_5.40a <- merge(all_combinations, plot_5.40a, all.x = TRUE)

# Fill NA values with 0
plot_5.40a$count[is.na(plot_5.40a$count)] <- 0
```

```{r}
subset_2 <- data %>% 
  filter(employment_type == "Employee") %>% 
  select(x41_all_maintenance, x37_all_collapsed, size_company_employee_work_1)

plot_5.52b <- subset_2 %>%
  drop_na(x41_all_maintenance, x37_all_collapsed, size_company_employee_work_1) %>%
  count(x41_all_maintenance, x37_all_collapsed, size_company_employee_work_1) %>%
  rename(count = n)

# Create a data frame with all combinations
all_combinations <- expand.grid(x41_all_maintenance = unique(plot_5.52b$x41_all_maintenance),
                                size_company_employee_work_1 = unique(plot_5.52b$size_company_employee_work_1),
                                x37_all_collapsed = unique(plot_5.52b$x37_all_collapsed))

# Merge with original data to get counts
plot_5.52b <- merge(all_combinations, plot_5.52b, all.x = TRUE)

# Fill NA values with 0
plot_5.52b$count[is.na(plot_5.52b$count)] <- 0
```
